blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — safe removal of contaminated gown and gloves, self-contamination prevention, and post-doffing hand hygiene
stem: A nurse is removing a contaminated gown and gloves after patient care. Which principle is most important when doffing this PPE?

options.A: Remove the gown and gloves before leaving the patient-care area, keep contaminated surfaces away from skin and clothing, and perform hand hygiene after doffing.
options.B: Remove the gloves in the room but keep the contaminated gown on until reaching a clean hallway area, then remove it and perform hand hygiene after disposal.
options.C: Remove the gown and gloves before leaving, but handle the contaminated front of the gown against the uniform as long as the gloves stay on until disposal.
options.D: Leave the room in the contaminated gown and gloves to transport encounter waste, then remove both at the nurses' station and perform hand hygiene.

rationale: A is correct. Current CDC Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices state that PPE other than respirators should be removed and discarded upon completion of the task before leaving the patient's room or care area and that healthcare personnel must be trained to remove and dispose of PPE in a manner that protects themselves, the patient, and others. CDC also requires hand hygiene immediately after glove removal. The current Isolation Precautions guidance emphasizes preventing contamination of skin and clothing during PPE removal and performing hand hygiene after PPE is removed. B is incorrect because carrying a contaminated gown into a clean hallway conflicts with removal before leaving the patient-care area. C is incorrect because contaminated gown surfaces should be handled in a way that avoids contact with the uniform or skin. D is incorrect because contaminated gown and gloves should not be worn into the nurses' station or other common areas before removal.
educational_objective: Doff contaminated gown and gloves before leaving the patient-care area, avoid contaminating skin or clothing during removal, discard the PPE appropriately, and perform hand hygiene afterward.
source_organization: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC); National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_document_title: CDC's Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices for Safe Healthcare Delivery in All Settings; Guideline for Isolation Precautions — Fundamental Elements Needed to Prevent Transmission; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan

Core Practices lines 77-88: hand hygiene indications include immediately after glove removal. The item intentionally tests these core principles rather than imposing one universal gown-versus-glove removal sequence.

correction_summary: Original Q0267 had a uniquely longest correct answer and an absolute-word distractor. The item was rebuilt with four plausible doffing workflows of similar length. The key focuses on CDC's stable core principles—remove non-respirator PPE before leaving the care area, prevent skin/clothing contamination, and perform hand hygiene—without inventing a single universally mandated gown-versus-glove sequence.

option_audit.A: Correct; integrates location of removal, self-contamination prevention, and hand hygiene without overclaiming a fixed sequence.
option_audit.B: Plausible partial doffing plan; incorrect because the contaminated gown is carried into a clean hallway instead of being removed before leaving the care area.
option_audit.C: Plausible sequence-focused plan; incorrect because allowing the contaminated gown surface to contact the uniform defeats contamination-prevention principles.
option_audit.D: Plausible waste-transport shortcut; incorrect because contaminated gown and gloves are carried into a common nurses' station rather than removed before leaving the care area.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on all/only/always/never-type wording as its sole cue.
cueing_audit.answer_length: Final option lengths: A 160, B 156, C 154, D 146 characters; the key is not conspicuously longer and all choices are realistic workflows.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives are operational doffing plans and differ in removal location or contamination control rather than obvious wording quality.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified in the pre-stage audit. B and D carry contaminated PPE outside the care area; C permits uniform contamination. Post-fetch adversarial reread remains required.
